# 油價反彈抵銷就業利多，借款人趕在數據前發債

## 荷莫茲通行成本再成焦點

荷莫茲海峽迅速重開的希望減弱，兩項原油指標均漲約5%，美債吐回週五就業數據帶來的漲幅。布蘭特上漲4.94%至$87.68，WTI上漲5.01%至$82.10。伊朗要求賠償，與美國又缺乏直接進展，通行仍未解決；中東至中國指標航線的超大型油輪租金，更接近每天$50萬。

2年期及5年期殖利率各升6個基點至4.25%、4.41%，10年期升7個基點至4.72%，30年期升6個基點至5.25%。10年期損益兩平通膨率升4個基點至2.29%，解釋超過一半漲幅，實質殖利率另升3個基點至2.43%。即使招聘轉弱，市場仍須為能源衝擊及政策可能持續限制性的風險付出補償。

克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁Beth Hammack進一步強化這項政策疑慮。這位7月異議官員認為，利率未對經濟形成有意義的限制，通膨不會自行回到2%，單次升息25個基點大概也沒有太大作用。她沒有指定終點，但認為可能需要數次調整，挑戰了週五就業減少就足以確立觀望理由的想法。

借款人仍取得資金。19家公司趕在本週通膨數據前，合計發行$276億美國投資級債。大盤幾乎不跌，高收益基金損失相對投資級存續期間也溫和。利率反轉明顯，卻未成為融資全面撤退。

## Hammack質疑一次升息是否足夠

曲線近乎平行上移，2s10s僅擴大1個基點至47，2s30s維持100。近一個月升幅仍隨年期增加：2年期4個基點、5年期11個基點、10年期16個基點、30年期19個基點。週一重啟短期政策風險，卻未消除更長期的融資負擔。

這次由通膨補償領先，不同於週五主要來自實質殖利率的反彈。10年期損益兩平通膨率2.29%，比一個月前高5個基點；實質殖利率2.43%，高11個基點，並回到8月6日水準。油價上升不只是市場價格逆轉，也在7月CPI前提高了等待通膨自行放緩的預期代價。

談判尚未帶來荷莫茲自由通行，川普也拒絕伊朗賠償要求。每天近$50萬的超大型油輪成本，為期貨漲勢提供實體市場對照。2年期殖利率由週五4.19%回到4.25%，10年期則超過8月6日收盤。新壓力來自能源供應及航運，而非美國需求突然加速的證據。

Hammack先前異議已表明她希望升息，這次新重點是幅度：一次25個基點可能無法明顯影響經濟，或須不只一次。她不願預設終點，因此即使勞動報告削弱立即行動理由，通膨數據仍決定緊縮的時間與程度。

就業組成的進一步分析，也使標題數字多了層次。7月就業減少23,000人，預估原為增加80,000人；其中地方政府就業減少60,000人，部分屬季節性，並與擴大教師編制的聯邦支持到期有關。民間就業近三個月平均增加40,000人，接近吸收新進勞動人口所需約50,000人的粗估。招聘弱，但私人部門比整體數字所顯示的更接近補充需求。

財政部可能調整年期，只提供部分抵銷。在官方措辭由評估未來發行「增加」改為「變化」後，BMO客戶調查61%預期，30年期標售規模下一步將下降。目前尚未宣布減量。轉向較短付息券可以改變供給落點，不能消除借款需求，尤其年度赤字接近$2兆。

財長Scott Bessent支持可能的年期調整，並試圖限制日圓干預外溢，仍未阻止30年期收在5.25%。投資人繼續面對通膨持續性、大量融資及其他國家殖利率競爭。名目美債付息券以原始面額計的成交達$6,980億、261,262筆，其中7至10年期$1,571億，20年以上$625億。交易活躍，但這是總成交量，不是方向性的淨流量歸因。

## 通膨前的擁擠發行日程仍順利成交

LQD跌0.55%，HYG跌0.16%，JNK跌0.17%。長天期AAA至A及BBB企業債指數各跌0.94%、0.86%，接近20年以上美債指數0.82%的跌幅。較大損失在存續期間，初級市場卻依然異常忙碌。

19家投資級發行人籌得$276億，是七個月最多，僅低於1月5日20家。上週已發行$800億、創今年第三高週量後，公司仍趕在通膨數據前融資。到週五，美國投資級今年已達$1.4兆，比2020年同期高9%；全球聯合承銷發行突破$5兆，比前次紀錄早一個多月。市場開著，發行人卻把少受事件干擾的窗口視為稀缺資源。

IBM以4年及8年期楓葉債籌得C$27.5億，為14年來首次加拿大交易。8年期以基準加120個基點定價，略低於初步討論。即使股價今年跌20%，投資人也擔心基礎設施與軟體業務，交易仍完成。這顯示需求不只在美國大型雲端業者，幣別與年期也能成為接觸不同買方的方式。

Lambda推出$9.17億貸款，支應Nvidia GPU及安裝，預先行銷訂單接近$20億。擬議價格最高為基準加375個基點、發行價99；4.4年期貸款約四年內全額攤還，另有提前贖回罰款。對快速淘汰的設備而言，還款安排很重要：買方取得的是明確本金回收路徑，而不只是AI需求曝險。

Global AI取得摩根大通牽頭的$4.41億資料中心融資。這家成立兩年的公司表示，有$62億合約收入，其中$10億容量已建成並交付。已簽約使用及完工容量，提供不同於純粹未來建設計畫的評估基礎，但執行仍重要。

監理處理方式可能使下一波交易更容易設計。SEC工作人員上月底認定，一大類與實體資料中心資產連結的債券，不必遵循傳統資產擔保交易的風險保留及揭露要求。這是工作人員指引，不是正式修法，也不涵蓋以房貸擔保的資料中心CMBS。但它移除了一項昂貴限制；該領域ABS年度發行由2020年$24億增至去年$155億，今年正朝另一紀錄前進。

潛在投資日程也在擴大。Nvidia與大型另類資產經理人規劃$5,000億AI基礎設施合作，名單包括Apollo、Blackstone、BlackRock及Brookfield。除了設備需求，這也代表未來債務與股權融資需求。消息後Nvidia跌2.9%、半導體指數跌2.94%，循環融資疑慮及更大的資本需求，限制了供應商表面上的利多。

因此，當日融資成功必須連同條件一起看。IBM進入不同幣別市場，Lambda以具吸引力的利差搭配攤還，廣泛投資級日程則趕在數據密集期前完成。較容易的證券化處理可能增加容量，也會增加競逐這些容量的證券；沒有一項結果保證下一筆能複製相同價格。

## 日本銀行摘要與保單解約，使日本展望更複雜

日本銀行7月30至31日會議新公布的意見摘要，顯示疑慮不限於立即升息的單一異議票。央行維持1%，僅高田創要求連續兩次升息；其他成員卻也警告，步伐可能超過市場預期，或要求對未來調整幅度保留彈性，包括更大動作。

重點已由把基礎通膨拉到2%，轉向避免超標。一名成員指出，即使1%仍低於估計1.1%至2.5%的中性區間。隔夜交換給予9月升息約三分之二機率，10月96%。正常化加快，可能使日本資產更能與外債競爭，即使美國殖利率也提高。

日圓盤中最弱時跌逾1%，美元兌日圓超過159，吐回7月31日美日操作約一半漲幅。Bessent的匯率穩定基金不到$2,200億，相較日本僅7月30日估計就投入$530億。FIMA可讓日本以逾$1兆美債持倉的一部分作擔保取得現金，但近期揭露顯示未使用。干預容量與備援機制，都尚未解決推動匯率的利差。

成長戰略大臣城內實為14年內向關鍵產業投入JPY370兆、以及每年估計JPY5兆的兩年消費稅減免計畫辯護。他認為生產力及日圓資產需求可改善永續性，支持日本銀行獨立，也不反對提早升息。但公私資金比例尚未說明，長期成長企圖仍與政府借款的不確定性並存。

保險負債帶來更直接的現金需求。更高收益替代產品出現後，2026年前五個月全產業解約給付年增約40%，超過JPY6兆、約$380億。明治安田第一季保費下降28%至JPY7,937億。壽險公司可能打算持有JGB配對長負債，但解約加速會迫使實現損失，或限制殖利率上升時的新買盤。

其他地區通膨放緩，使部分央行有更多空間。挪威7月排除能源的核心CPI維持2.7%，低於預估2.9%及央行6月預測3.3%。隔夜交換將本週會議緊縮定價由6個基點降至2個基點，9月仍有15個基點。本國商品與服務加速，電價又使整體通膨升至3.0%，高於預估2.8%。立即行動的理由，減弱程度大於秋季展望。

丹麥通膨由1.9%降至1.7%；中國CPI年增由1%降至0.5%，生產者通膨由4.1%降至3.5%。中國5年以上政策銀行債指數漲0.05%，美元存續期間卻下跌。這些數據支撐本地曲線，未代表全球政策走向相同。

羅馬尼亞維持歐盟最高的6.5%基準利率，先前油價及管制價格使5、6月通膨超過10%。政治爭議拖延取得歐盟資金所需改革，利率已近兩年不變。穆迪維持最低投資級，主要評等機構的負向展望，仍使焦點落在政府效能及減赤。本地及美元債上漲，但評等暫時保住，本身不會創造降息空間。

歐元區調查把2026成長由0.5%升至0.8%，幾乎完全來自第2季GDP增加0.4%、為預估兩倍。第3季仍估0.2%，之後僅逐步改善。已實現成長較好降低立即衰退疑慮，並不是未來展望同步上修，尤其能源又轉貴。

## 國營相關企業，支持方式各不相同

EMB跌0.42%，15年期以上新興美元主權債指數跌0.29%，美元指數漲0.19%至99.79。更高美國實質殖利率、美元轉強及約5%油價漲幅，使共同環境較差。更具體的信用問題，在於本地政策空間，以及誰願提供資本給壓力中的國營相關企業。

菲律賓總裁Eli Remolona表示，央行準備採取所需程度的緊縮，使通膨回到目標。此前第2季成長意外降至2.3%，消費與投資收縮。通膨仍6.2%，超過政府目標兩倍。活動放緩減少立即行動壓力，副總裁Zeno Abenoja也說核心通膨可能已趨平，但弱成長本身沒有提供明確寬鬆路徑。

Braskem債權人包括Elliott及Contrarian，正要求國家控制的Petrobras在8月24日庭外重整期限前，提供股權、營運資金或次順位債。Petrobras抗拒，部分因持股增加可能須合併Braskem債務。至少三分之一債務持有人支持，才可避免司法重整；穆迪已將現有法院暫停償付安排視為違約。2030年債利差約為美債加1,900個基點。

債權人反提案改善庭外協議機會，但股東支持的形式與金額仍未解決。巴西選舉年增加政治敏感度，並未把Braskem義務變成主權債。Petrobras出資可改善子公司，卻可能把槓桿或資金需求轉到國家控制的股東身上。

智利對Codelco做了更明確的移轉選擇。政府允許保留全部2025年$24.2億獲利，為公司五十多年來首次保留全年盈餘。債務約$250億創紀錄，產量近28年低點，保留現金是要在不再增借下支應復甦。

Codelco仍須把銷售額10%支付國家，因此決策以部分當期財政收入，交換更強的企業資產負債表，結果取決於投資紀律及產量恢復。相較Braskem尚有爭議的支持方案，這是已確定的現金緩衝。兩者顯示，與國家有關聯，本身並不能回答誰承擔融資負擔。

## 黃金與油價上漲，科技股回落

WTI收$82.10、布蘭特$87.68，均漲約5%，10年期損益兩平通膨率升4個基點。S&P 500僅跌0.06%，VIX漲3.76%至仍受控的15.46。能源重新定價，尚未造成同等幅度的大盤風險偏好下降。

科技更弱，Nasdaq 100跌0.34%，半導體跌2.94%，Nvidia在擬議$5,000億基礎設施合作報導後跌2.9%。更大投資承諾支持潛在容量需求，也引發循環融資及所需資本的問題，與貸款人關注擔保品、攤還及簽約使用一致。

即使美元及10年期實質殖利率提高，黃金仍漲2.69%至$4,457.50。美元當日上漲後，一個月仍跌1.17%，高收益也優於投資級存續期間。地緣政治及融資不確定性提高，卻不像全面搶奪美元流動性。

## CPI、季度再融資與Lambda最終條件

週三7月CPI仍預估整體月增0.1%、前值下降0.4%，核心月增0.2%、年增2.5%。服務普遍較弱，會反駁Hammack需要多次升息的論點；明顯高於預期，則讓9月決策再次成為焦點。荷莫茲持續受阻與高運費，也會影響這份報告衡量期間之外的通膨路徑。

$1,250億季度再融資由週二$580億3年期開始，週三$420億10年期，週四$250億30年期。10年期接在CPI之後，實質殖利率目前2.43%；長債則接續5.25%收盤。交易商集中度、讓利及後續殖利率，將顯示當前價格能否吸收已宣布供給。未來長債減量的期待不能取代真實需求，尤其日圓若再跌破160，引發新干預疑問時。

Lambda承諾截止週四。最終利差、發行價及4.4年期全額攤還結構是否保留，將顯示預先行銷訂單能否轉成擬議融資。後續資料中心ABS與企業債也會檢驗，SEC處理放寬是否增加供給、卻不再壓抑科技舊券。次級交易穩定，代表新條件下有容量；擴大利差或配售後損失，則顯示投資日程帶來更高持續成本。

overall_summary.headline: 油價反彈抵銷就業利多，借款人趕在數據前發債
overall_summary.session_narrative:
談判尚未恢復荷莫茲自由通行，布蘭特漲4.94%、WTI漲5.01%，超大型油輪成本接近每天$50萬。10年期殖利率升7個基點至4.72%，其中通膨補償增加4個基點，實質殖利率增加3個基點。

Hammack認為單次25個基點可能無法明顯限制經濟。就業組成則為週五弱勢標題補充層次，未來長債減量仍只是期待。CPI及季度再融資標售都尚未到來。

19家美國投資級發行人籌得$276億。IBM重返加拿大，Lambda推出攤還型GPU貸款，SEC工作人員指引可能放寬部分資料中心ABS結構。日本政策及壽險現金需求使外資更複雜；Codelco取得明確盈餘緩衝，Braskem股東支持卻仍有爭議。

section_summaries.summary: 荷莫茲通行未解，推升油價及美債殖利率兩個組成。Hammack認為或需不只一次升息，資本市場仍開放。

section_summaries.section_title: Hammack質疑一次升息是否足夠

long_thesis.english_markdown:
# Oil's rebound erases the payroll rally as borrowers rush to issue

## Hormuz costs return to the foreground

Treasuries gave back Friday's labor-led gains as fading hopes for a quick Hormuz reopening sent both crude benchmarks up about 5%. Brent rose 4.94% to $87.68 and WTI gained 5.01% to $82.10. Iran's compensation demands and little direct progress with the US left passage unresolved, while the cost of hiring a supertanker on the benchmark Middle East-to-China route approached $500,000 a day.

Two- and five-year yields each rose 6 basis points to 4.25% and 4.41%, the ten-year rose 7 to 4.72%, and the 30-year rose 6 to 5.25%. The ten-year breakeven widened 4 basis points to 2.29%, accounting for more than half the move; the real yield rose 3 basis points to 2.43%. The market was again paying for both an energy shock and the possibility that policy would have to remain restrictive despite weaker hiring.

Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack sharpened that policy concern. The July dissenter said rates were not meaningfully restraining the economy, inflation would not return to 2% by itself, and one quarter-point increase probably would not do much. She did not specify an endpoint, but her argument for some number of increases challenged the idea that Friday's payroll loss had settled the case for patience.

Borrowers nevertheless continued to find money. Nineteen companies sold $27.6 billion of US investment-grade bonds ahead of the week's inflation reports. Broad equities barely fell, and high-yield fund losses were modest compared with investment-grade duration. The rates reversal was substantial; it did not amount to a general withdrawal of financing.

## Hammack questions whether one increase would be enough

The nearly parallel selloff steepened 2s10s by only 1 basis point to 47 and left 2s30s at 100. Monthly yield increases still grew with maturity: 4 basis points at two years, 11 at five, 16 at ten and 19 at 30. Monday renewed near-term policy risk without removing the longer financing burden.

Inflation compensation led, unlike Friday's mainly real-yield-driven rally. The ten-year breakeven at 2.29% was 5 basis points above a month earlier; the real yield at 2.43% was 11 basis points higher and back at its August 6 level. Higher oil was not simply reversing a market price. It was raising the expected cost of waiting for inflation to subside before the July CPI release.

Negotiations had not produced free passage through Hormuz, and President Donald Trump rejected Iran's compensation demands. Supertanker costs near $500,000 a day gave a physical counterpart to the futures rally. The two-year yield returned to 4.25% from Friday's 4.19%, while the ten-year exceeded its August 6 close. The new pressure came from energy supply and shipping rather than evidence that US demand had suddenly accelerated.

Hammack's earlier dissent had established that she wanted an increase. Her new emphasis was on scale: a single 25-basis-point move probably would not materially affect the economy, and more than one might be needed. She declined to prejudge the endpoint. That leaves inflation data central to both the timing and extent of tightening, even after the labor report weakened the case for immediate action.

Further analysis of payrolls supplied a qualification to that report. July employment fell 23,000 against an 80,000 consensus, but a 60,000 decline in local-government jobs was partly seasonal and linked to expiring federal support for expanded teaching staffs. Private payrolls averaged 40,000 over three months, near a rough 50,000 estimate of the pace needed to absorb new labor-force entrants. Hiring was weak, but the private economy was closer to replacement pace than the aggregate headline suggested.

Treasury's possible maturity changes offered only a partial offset. In a BMO client poll, 61% expected the next move in 30-year auction sizes to be a decrease, following the shift in official language from evaluating future issuance “increases” to “changes.” No cut has been announced. Moving financing toward shorter coupons could alter where supply lands, not eliminate the borrowing need, particularly with annual deficits near $2 trillion.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's support for possible maturity adjustments and efforts to limit yen-intervention spillovers did not keep the 30-year below 5.25%. Investors still faced inflation persistence, a heavy financing requirement and competing foreign yields. Nominal Treasury coupon activity totaled $698.0 billion of original-face value across 261,262 trades, including $157.1 billion at seven to ten years and $62.5 billion beyond 20 years. Trading was active, but these are gross activity measures, not a directional flow attribution.

## A crowded calendar clears before inflation data

LQD fell 0.55%, HYG 0.16% and JNK 0.17%. Long-maturity AAA–A and BBB corporate indexes lost 0.94% and 0.86%, close to the 0.82% decline in the Treasury index beyond 20 years. The larger losses were in duration, while the primary calendar remained unusually busy.

Nineteen investment-grade issuers raised $27.6 billion, the most borrowers in seven months and just below the 20 on January 5. They accelerated ahead of inflation data after last week's $80 billion, the third-highest weekly total of 2026. By Friday, US investment-grade issuance had reached $1.4 trillion, 9% ahead of the comparable 2020 pace. Global syndicated issuance crossed $5 trillion more than a month ahead of the previous record. Issuers were using an open market while treating quiet event windows as scarce.

IBM broadened its funding with C$2.75 billion of four- and eight-year Maple bonds, its first Canadian transaction in 14 years. The eight-year tranche priced 120 basis points over its benchmark, slightly inside initial discussion. It cleared despite a 20% year-to-date equity decline and concerns about its infrastructure and software businesses. The result showed demand outside the US hyperscaler calendar, with currency and maturity providing another way to reach buyers.

Lambda launched a $917 million loan to finance Nvidia GPUs and installation, with premarketing orders nearing $2 billion. Proposed pricing was as much as 375 basis points over the benchmark at 99. The 4.4-year loan would amortize fully over roughly four years and include an early-redemption penalty. The repayment schedule is important for equipment that can lose technological value quickly: lenders were being offered a defined path to getting principal back, not just exposure to AI demand.

Global AI raised a $441 million JPMorgan-led facility for data centers. The two-year-old company cited $6.2 billion of contracted revenue, including $1 billion of capacity already built and delivered. Contracted use and completed capacity give lenders a different basis for assessing the financing from a purely prospective buildout, although execution still matters.

Regulatory treatment could make the next wave easier to structure. SEC staff concluded late last month that a major subset of bonds tied to physical data-center assets need not follow the risk-retention and disclosure requirements applied to conventional asset-backed deals. This is staff guidance, not a formal rule change, and it does not cover mortgage-backed data-center CMBS. It nonetheless removes a costly constraint in a sector whose annual ABS issuance grew from $2.4 billion in 2020 to $15.5 billion last year and is headed for another record.

The prospective investment pipeline is also expanding. Nvidia and large alternative managers were planning a $500 billion AI-infrastructure partnership, with Apollo, Blackstone, BlackRock and Brookfield among the named participants. It represents future debt and equity funding needs as well as demand for equipment. Nvidia fell 2.9% and the semiconductor index lost 2.94% after the report, with circular-financing concerns and the larger capital requirement tempering the apparent benefit to suppliers.

The day's successful financings therefore need to be read with their terms. IBM reached a different currency market, Lambda paired an attractive spread with amortization, and a broad high-grade calendar cleared before a data-heavy period. Easier securitization treatment may add capacity, but also more securities competing for it. None of those results guarantees that the next transaction can repeat the same pricing.

## BOJ minutes and insurer surrenders complicate Japan's outlook

The newly released summary of the BOJ's July 30–31 meeting showed concern beyond the single dissent for an immediate increase. The bank held at 1%, with only Hajime Takata seeking a back-to-back hike. Other members nevertheless warned that the pace could exceed market expectations or urged flexibility over the size of future moves, including larger adjustments.

The emphasis had shifted from lifting underlying inflation to 2% toward preventing an overshoot. One member noted that even 1% remained below the estimated 1.1%–2.5% neutral range. Overnight swaps assigned roughly a two-thirds chance to September tightening and 96% by October. Faster normalization could make Japanese assets more competitive with foreign bonds even as US yields rose.

The yen weakened more than 1% at its intraday low, traded beyond 159 per dollar and erased about half the rally from the July 31 US-Japan operation. Bessent's Exchange Stabilization Fund holds less than $220 billion, compared with an estimated $53 billion deployed by Japan on July 30 alone. FIMA could turn part of Japan's more than $1 trillion Treasury holdings into cash against collateral, but recent disclosures showed no use. Neither intervention capacity nor the backstop had resolved the rate differential driving the currency.

Growth Strategy Minister Minoru Kiuchi defended plans to channel JPY370 trillion into critical sectors over 14 years and cut sales tax for two years at an estimated annual cost near JPY5 trillion. He argued that productivity and demand for yen assets would improve sustainability, endorsed BOJ independence and did not oppose an early increase. The public/private financing split remains unspecified, leaving the long-run growth ambition alongside uncertainty over government borrowing.

Insurance liabilities create a more immediate demand for cash. Sector-wide payouts on surrendered policies rose about 40% year on year in the first five months of 2026 to more than JPY6 trillion, or $38 billion, as higher-yielding alternatives became available. Meiji Yasuda's first-quarter premiums fell 28% to JPY793.7 billion. Insurers may intend to hold JGBs against long liabilities, but faster surrenders can force them to realize losses or limit new purchases just as yields increase.

Elsewhere, softer inflation gave some central banks more room. Norway's July core CPI excluding energy held at 2.7%, below the 2.9% consensus and Norges Bank's June projection of 3.3%. Overnight swaps cut the tightening priced for this week's meeting from 6 basis points to 2, although 15 remained by September. Domestic goods and services accelerated, and electricity lifted headline inflation to 3.0%, above 2.8% expected. The case for an immediate move weakened more than the autumn outlook.

Denmark's inflation slowed from 1.9% to 1.7%. China's CPI eased from 1% to 0.5% year on year and producer inflation from 4.1% to 3.5%; its five-year-plus policy-bank bond index rose 0.05% while dollar duration fell. Those readings supported local curves without implying a common global policy direction.

Romania kept its benchmark at 6.5%, the EU's highest, after oil and administered prices pushed inflation above 10% in May and June. Rates had been steady for almost two years as political disputes delayed reforms needed for EU funds. Moody's retained the lowest investment-grade rating, while negative outlooks among the major assessors kept attention on government effectiveness and deficit reduction. Local and dollar bonds gained, but a rating reprieve did not itself create room to ease.

A euro-area survey raised the 2026 growth forecast from 0.5% to 0.8%, almost entirely because second-quarter GDP rose 0.4%, twice expectations. The third-quarter estimate stayed at 0.2%, followed by only gradual improvement. Better realized activity reduced immediate recession concern; it was not a corresponding upgrade to future growth, particularly with energy costs rising again.

## State-company support takes different forms

EMB fell 0.42% and the 15-year-plus EM dollar sovereign index lost 0.29% as the Dollar Index rose 0.19% to 99.79. Higher US real yields, a firmer dollar and roughly 5% oil gains made the common backdrop less favorable. The more specific credit questions concerned local policy room and who would supply capital to stressed state-linked businesses.

Philippine Governor Eli Remolona said the central bank was prepared to tighten as much as necessary to return inflation to target. That warning followed an unexpected slowdown in second-quarter growth to 2.3%, as consumption and investment contracted. Inflation remained 6.2%, more than twice the government's target. Slower activity reduced immediate pressure to act, and Deputy Governor Zeno Abenoja said core inflation may have plateaued, but weak growth alone did not give the bank a clear easing path.

Braskem's creditors, including Elliott and Contrarian, pressed state-controlled Petrobras for equity, working capital or junior debt before an August 24 out-of-court restructuring deadline. Petrobras resisted partly because greater ownership could require consolidating Braskem's debt. Support from holders of at least one-third of debt is needed to avoid judicial recovery, and Moody's treated the existing court standstill as a default. The 2030 bonds traded around 1,900 basis points over Treasuries.

A creditor counterproposal improved the prospect of an out-of-court agreement, but the form and amount of shareholder support remained unresolved. The Brazilian election year adds political sensitivity without turning Braskem's obligation into sovereign debt. Capital supplied by Petrobras could improve the subsidiary's position while transferring leverage or funding demands to a state-controlled shareholder.

Chile made a more definite transfer choice for Codelco. The government allowed the company to retain all $2.42 billion of its 2025 profit, its first full-year earnings retention in more than 50 years. Debt was at a record near $25 billion and production near a 28-year low. Keeping the cash is intended to finance recovery without adding more borrowing.

Codelco still pays 10% of sales to the state. The decision therefore exchanges some current fiscal revenue for a stronger company balance sheet, with the outcome depending on investment discipline and production recovery. Unlike Braskem's disputed support package, this is a defined cash buffer. The two cases show why state association is not itself an answer to who bears the financing burden.

## Gold and oil rise while technology slips

WTI at $82.10 and Brent at $87.68, both up about 5%, accompanied a 4-basis-point rise in ten-year breakevens. The S&P 500 fell only 0.06%, while VIX rose 3.76% to a still-contained 15.46. The energy repricing had not produced a comparably large reduction in broad equity risk appetite.

Technology was weaker. The Nasdaq 100 declined 0.34%, semiconductors lost 2.94% and Nvidia fell 2.9% after the proposed $500 billion infrastructure partnership was reported. A larger investment commitment supports potential capacity demand, but raises questions about circular funding and the capital still needed to deliver it. That concern fits the attention lenders are paying to collateral, amortization and contracted use.

Gold gained 2.69% to $4,457.50 despite a firmer dollar and higher ten-year real yield. The dollar's daily rise still left it down 1.17% over a month, and high yield outperformed investment-grade duration. Geopolitical and financing uncertainty increased, but the moves did not resemble a broad scramble for dollar liquidity.

## CPI, refunding and Lambda's final terms

Wednesday's July CPI forecast remains a 0.1% headline increase after a 0.4% decline, with core rising 0.2% monthly and 2.5% yearly. Broadly softer services would counter Hammack's argument for repeated increases. A material upside surprise would bring the September decision back into sharper focus. Continued Hormuz disruption and high freight costs would matter for the inflation path beyond the report's measurement window as well.

The $125 billion refunding begins with Tuesday's $58 billion three-year auction, followed by $42 billion of ten-year notes on Wednesday and $25 billion of 30-year bonds on Thursday. The ten-year sale follows CPI with real yields now at 2.43%; the long sale follows a 5.25% close. Dealer concentration, concessions and subsequent yields will show whether current prices absorb the announced supply. Expectations of smaller future long-bond auctions are not a substitute for that demand, especially if renewed yen weakness beyond 160 raises intervention questions again.

Lambda commitments are due Thursday. Its final spread, issue price and retention of the 4.4-year fully amortizing structure will show whether premarketing orders translate into the proposed financing. Subsequent data-center ABS and corporate deals will also test whether easier SEC treatment expands supply without further repricing outstanding technology bonds. Stable secondary trading would suggest capacity at the new terms; wider pricing or post-allocation losses would show a higher continuing cost of the investment pipeline.
